extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of moral philosophy; readers of Kant's Groundwork/Metaphysics of Morals
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative standards and methodological principles from Kant's discussion of pure practical reason (postulates, faith, and the methodology for making moral law subjectively motivating). Useful for interpreting Kantian moral theory and for pedagogy on moral motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of pure cognition practically requires an a priori purpose (summum bonum)
rubrics_metrics.description: To extend a pure cognition practically there must be an a priori purpose given — an end as object (of the will) — which, independently of theological principle, is presented as practically necessary by a categorical imperative; in this case that end is the summum bonum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the condition for practical extension of cognition: a practical law that determines the will directly. Without such an a priori purpose pure cognition cannot be extended practically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postulation of freedom, immortality, and God as practical necessities
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical reason, in requiring the possibility of the summum bonum, postulates three theoretical conceptions — freedom, immortality, and God — giving them objective reality for practical purposes, though they have no corresponding intuition and are not cognitions for speculative reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These postulates are justified because practical reason requires them for the possibility of its object (the summum bonum). They render the otherwise problematical ideas assertorially real for practical employment, but they do not enable theoretical (synthetic) knowledge about these objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical postulates grant objective reality but do not extend theoretical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Although practical reason can justify admitting the reality of ideas (by showing they have objects necessary for practical ends), this admission does not make synthetical propositions about them possible nor extend speculative knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use postulates only to secure the objects of practical reason (e.g., for moral action). They clear up and secure practical use but cannot be turned into grounds for theoretical claims about supersensible objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of categories to think ideas of reason for practical purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure concepts of the understanding (categories) are required in every employment of reason to conceive an object; they can be applied to ideas of reason (which cannot be given in experience) so as to think those objects generally, even without intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because categories originate a priori in the understanding and signify objects in general, they can be legitimately applied to the practical postulates to prevent the categories from being empty in this context — but this application still does not yield theoretical cognition of supersensible objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid anthropomorphism in determining predicates of God
rubrics_metrics.description: When predicates taken from our nature (understanding and will) are used to determine the ideas of God, immortality, etc., we must abstract from empirical, psychological attributes; otherwise we would sensualize or anthropomorphize pure rational ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain only those attributes of understanding and will that are required for conceiving a moral law; do not treat such predicates as yielding a theoretical or speculative knowledge of supersensible beings. This is an anti-pattern: letting psychological observations contaminate pure rational conceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept of God belongs to morals rather than physics/metaphysics
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of God, insofar as it serves as the basis for the summum bonum and moral order, originates in practical reason (morals) and not in physics or speculative metaphysics; speculative proofs of God's existence are impossible because they would require omniscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to derive God's existence from empirical or purely speculative premises about the world; instead, recognize that the moral law determines the conception of a Supreme Being necessary for the possibility of the summum bonum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish hypothesis (speculative) from postulate (practical) in requirements of reason
rubrics_metrics.description: A want or requirement of pure speculative reason leads only to a hypothesis (rational opinion), whereas a want of pure practical reason gives rise to a postulate (a necessary presupposition) because it is grounded in duty — e.g., the postulation of God, freedom, immortality for the summum bonum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat practical postulates as more than merely permissible hypotheses: they are practically necessary assumptions founded on the objective demand of duty. This is a normative criterion for justifying certain beliefs in moral contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith of pure practical reason is voluntary and not a commanded belief
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'faith' grounded in pure practical reason is not itself commanded; it is a voluntary determination of judgement (a maxim of belief) that is conducive to the moral purpose and harmonizes with theoretical reason, though it may waver in the well-disposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mistake the practical justification for a command to believe; rather, endorse faith as a permissible and morally grounded stance that one may adopt to promote the summum bonum. It cannot be legitimately prohibited by speculative objections alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of cognition are adaptively wise for moral development
rubrics_metrics.description: Human ignorance and the absence of certain knowledge about God, immortality, etc., are beneficial: had we full intuitive knowledge, moral actions would tend to be mechanical (done from fear or hope) rather than from duty, and so lack moral worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the epistemic limitations as conditions that allow genuine moral disposition (acting from duty) to arise. This is an evaluative standard for assessing moral psychology and educational design: avoid making moral demands so transparently enforced that inner moral worth is obviated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology of pure practical reason: make objective laws subjectively practical
rubrics_metrics.description: By 'methodology' Kant means the mode by which laws of pure practical reason can be given access to the human mind and made subjectively practical — i.e., how to make objectively valid moral laws become the actual springs of action in subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proper methodological aim is not merely to teach laws abstractly but to present them so their objective necessity and direct conception (the law itself) become the springs of action. This rules out pedagogical approaches that produce legality without morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral worth requires acting from duty (respect for law), not merely conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The determining principles of the will that make maxims properly moral are the direct conception of the law and the objective necessity of obeying it as duty; actions have moral worth only when motivated by respect for the law, not by inclinations, fear, or self-interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess moral actions by whether they arise from respect for duty. Beware the anti-pattern where legality (externally conforming action) is produced without the spirit of the law in the mind — such actions lack moral worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical sequence: preparatory guidance followed by presentation of the pure moral motive
rubrics_metrics.description: For uncultivated or degraded minds, some preparatory guidance (appealing to self-interest or fear) may be necessary to bring them into moral habits; but this must be followed by presenting the pure moral motive so that morality of character (acting from duty) is developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use utilitarian or prudential inducements only as temporary leading-strings; the ultimate pedagogical normative criterion is to cultivate respect for the law so that morality becomes a stable character trait rather than mere compliance.
